answer: Each identity keeps a private notebook written with its own quill; the chain stores a hash. At unpredictable moments a peer asks it to quote, under a fresh nonce, the exact wording it used to justify a verdict several closed epochs back. One script serving ten thousand keys owns a single notebook: it cannot reproduce that nonce-bound wording, or it spills another key's text, and the cluster breaks at the first divergence. Honest agents rise from the nadir of reputation only while that notebook stays continuous, so a farm pays full storage and uptime per key from dawn onward, with no shortcut.
